summary:
Project Axle is an interactive web-based strategy and simulation game that challenges players to design and sustain a human survival mission on Mars. Built around official NASA systems engineering principles, the game guides players through the real-world mission lifecycle, from defining a Concept of Operations and balancing tight mass and power budgets to managing the four core mission segments consisting of Launch, Space, Ground, and User.

Players sequence critical habitat operations, such as atmospheric sealing, power grid deployment, and biological nutrient production, and respond in real time to Martian environmental hazards like regional dust storms and radiation spikes. By turning complex aerospace engineering frameworks into an accessible, hands-on survival challenge, Project Mars 101 addresses the mission concept challenge while educating students and the public on the meticulous planning, resource trade-offs, and scientific rigor required to keep astronauts alive on another planet.
details:
Project AXLE

What does it do or how does it work?

Project AXLE is an interactive web-based strategy and simulation game that guides players through the real-world process of designing and executing a human survival mission on Mars. Players act as mission architects, moving through official NASA systems engineering phases by defining a Concept of Operations (ConOps), managing mass and power budgets, and navigating the four core mission segments:

  • Launch Segment: Players select heavy-lift launch vehicles or commercial cargo landers to transport habitat modules, life support systems, and rovers to Mars within strict mass and volume limits.
  • Space Segment (The Martian Habitat): Players manage surface landers, rovers, and onboard scientific or life-support instruments, such as biological nutrient production packs and water recyclers, to sustain the crew.
  • Ground Segment (Mission Control): Players control what material is sent and review the available resources 
  • User Segment (The Martian Crew & Scientists): Players oversee the astronauts living in the habitat as they execute daily operational procedures, process life-support data, and conduct science experiments.

What benefits and intended impact does it have?

The project bridges the gap between complex aerospace engineering and accessible education. Its intended impact is to teach students, space enthusiasts, and the public about the meticulous planning, resource trade-offs, and scientific rigor required for deep space exploration, turning abstract NASA documentation into an engaging hands-on challenge.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Developed for a 48-hour hackathon sprint, this project utilizes a lightweight and responsive web stack. We used HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and JavaScript for the front-end dashboard interface, interactive drag-and-drop ConOps timeline builders, and real-time simulation logic.

How is your project creative and what factors did your team consider?

Rather than relying on standard survival-crafting tropes, Project AXLE creatively applies actual NASA systems engineering frameworks (such as NPR 7123.1 guidelines for ConOps) directly into gameplay mechanics. Our team carefully considered time constraints, ensuring that the user interface remains intuitive and modular so that players can experience authentic mission design without getting bogged down by overly dense calculations.

Why did we make this game?

Amongst us there are members who are avid gamers and thought, why not create a survival like game that is based on Mars? With no background in game programming we decided that this idea is worth a shot. We are well aware it's possible there are similar games out there to ours but this is ours, and we attempted to get it as close to our vision as possible with the skills and talent we have.

This game shows the consequences of our actions, rewards when you succeed to survive. Indirectly it teaches what each mission system contribute to keep us alive and sometimes sacrifices has to be made in order to move forward. With unexpected weather forecasts to keep players on their toes and make sure their space station lasts
